Dürer or Goltzius? Mystery surrounding Renaissance engraving unveiled at Astana exhibition
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:42:56 UTC
01:42:56 KST

Dürer or Goltzius? Mystery surrounding Renaissance engraving unveiled at Astana exhibition
An exhibition exploring the legacy of German Renaissance master Albrecht Dürer opened at LM Kulanshi Art Space on October 29, featuring a mysterious engraving whose authorship remains disputed, Qazinform News Agency reports.
Titled “Dürer: Metamorphoses of Alchemy”, the exhibition brings together graphic works, illustrations from early printed books, historical portraits, alchemical treatises and materials exploring the relationship between art, science and philosophy during the Northern Renaissance.
The opening ceremony was attended by Archbishop George Panamthundil, Apostolic Nuncio to Kazakhstan, who reflected on the importance of art in an increasingly technology-driven world.
“In a world increasingly dominated by technology, artificial intelligence and instant information, we need this transforming power of art more than ever,” he said.
“Technology can provide us with information, but art invites us to contemplation. Technology helps us to find answers. Art often helps us discover better questions,” the archbishop added.
Panamthundil also drew a parallel between the exhibition’s theme of transformation and Astana’s development, describing the Kazakh capital as a city that had evolved from the vast steppe into a meeting place of cultures and ideas.
Mystery behind the Pietà engraving
Leila Makhat, founder of Kulanshi Art Center and curator of the exhibition, revealed that the project had been in preparation for more than a year and a half, with exhibits collected from different countries.
According to Makhat, one of the exhibition’s greatest mysteries concerns the authorship of Pietà, an engraving depicting the Virgin Mary mourning Jesus Christ.
“Was it made by Dürer, as it is written in many analogues, or was it made by his fan and copyist Goltzius?” she asked.
Makhat explained that expert opinions remain divided, with some publications attributing the work to Dürer and others to Dutch engraver Hendrick Goltzius (1558-1617), who was known for his ability to imitate the styles of earlier masters.
“I think we will not be able to answer this question, because artists and experts are divided exactly into two camps,” she said.
Nevertheless, the curator suggested that the artistic and emotional significance of the work goes beyond the question of authorship.
“I think the point is in the beauty. I think the point is that these stories touch everyone, no matter what religion a person belongs to,” Makhat said.
The exhibition examines how Dürer (1471-1528), one of the leading figures of the Northern Renaissance, combined artistic mastery with an interest in mathematics, geometry, human proportions and the natural world.
Alchemy serves as a central metaphor for transformation, illustrating how artists turned ordinary materials into works of art and transformed observation into knowledge.
Makhat also highlighted Dürer’s theoretical writings, noting that the exhibition features a page from one of his treatises. She said further details about his life, artistic methods and lesser-known biographical facts would be explored during lectures associated with the exhibition.
Concluding his remarks, Panamthundil encouraged visitors to rediscover their sense of curiosity.
“Because the greatest discovery is not always something new in the world, sometimes it is a new way of looking at the world we already know,” he said.
Earlier, Qazinform reported on the “GLOCAL” exhibition at Kazakhstan’s National Museum, featuring photographs and stories of 30 people connected to UN-supported programs.

2027 Dakar Rally to be held in Morocco and Portugal: organisers
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:42:33 UTC
01:42:33 KST

Breadcrumb
2027 Dakar Rally to be held in Morocco and Portugal, organisers say
The 2027 Dakar Rally will be held in Morocco following a prologue and first stage in Portugal, organisers Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) said on Friday, five days after announcing that the event would not take place in Saudi Arabia due to security concerns.
The conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels reignited in July, with Houthis firing drones and rockets at Saudi airports, oil sites and shipping. Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes inside Yemen.
"The Algarve will host the prologue and the first special stage. Morocco, with the aim of exploring its territory in its entirety, from north to far south, will host 11 stages and a rest day in Agadir," ASO said in a statement.
The 49th Dakar Rally, initially scheduled to run from January 1 to January 15, will take place from January 9 to January 23, subject to approval by the FIA's World Motor Sport Council.
"The relocated 49th edition of the Dakar will meet the sporting standards that have always made it the most demanding rally-raid event," Dakar director David Castera said.
"Despite the short timeframe we have had to work with, we have designed a true Dakar."
Dakar 2027 will cover a distance of 7,824 km, including 4,341 km of special stages, from Loule-Faro to Marrakech.
"We all worked to make sure this Dakar could take place. The fact that we’re doing it in two months doesn’t mean it will be a watered-down Dakar," Castera told reporters on Friday.
The Dakar Rally will return to Saudi Arabia, which has hosted the event since 2020, in 2028.
It will be held in Africa for the first time since 2007. The 2008 edition was cancelled the day before the start due to security concerns.
"I thought it was good for the Dakar to return a bit to its roots, that is, to start from Europe and head towards the African continent. We wanted a more international dimension, which is why we’re starting in Portugal," Castera added.
The event started in 1978 as a race from Paris across the Sahara to the Senegalese capital Dakar in West Africa, and has long been regarded as the world's toughest motorsport challenge.
It was staged in South America between 2009 and 2019 after being moved from Africa due to security reasons.

An alleged Turkish crime syndicate leader who survived an assassination attempt some two weeks earlier was fatally shot inside a Spanish hospital room early Thursday in a highly coordinated hit.
Catalonia’s regional police force, the Mossos d'Esquadra, announced they are investigating the fatal shooting of an admitted patient at a hospital in Tarragona. While police placed the case under a judicial secrecy order, a law enforcement source confirmed to OCCRP that the victim was Mekin Büyükdeniz, a member of the Ten Brothers criminal group.
According to Turkish media, the Küçükçekmece Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office formally named Büyükdeniz in prosecutorial filings as the operational leader of the so-called “10 Brothers” gang. In the organizational hierarchy documented in the prosecutor's investigation, the syndicate was identified as a family-centered armed network directed by the Büyükdeniz brothers.
The meticulously timed execution occurred around 3:15 a.m., just ten minutes after Büyükdeniz was transferred from intensive care to a regular room on the hospital's fifth floor, Sabah reported. To create a diversion, an accomplice allegedly distracted hospital security by sexually harassing a nurse. This allowed a helmeted gunman on an electric scooter to slip through the emergency room entrance, go directly to Büyükdeniz's room, and shoot him three times in the head and body in front of his wife. Following the attack, his wife was placed under police protection, the outlet noted.
Büyükdeniz was recovering at the Joan XXIII Hospital following an October 16 drive-by shooting in the nearby coastal town of Salou, where a gunman fired 10 shots and wounded him in the legs. According to Sabah, Büyükdeniz had refused to give a statement to police and brought in a private bodyguard from Turkey. Assessing that the security risk had dropped, local law enforcement removed his police protection just before the attack.
Following Thursday’s assassination, the hitman reportedly escaped through the hospital's garbage collection area. Catalan police immediately activated an emergency protocol, setting up roadblocks across Tarragona and Catalonia to hunt for the suspects, Sabah reported.
The Mossos d'Esquadra confirmed that their Criminal Investigation Division (DIC) has taken over the probe. Emergency services also activated a psychological support team for the hospital staff.

New MOKH Module for Autonomous Navigation Appears in Geran Drones – DIU
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:41:22 UTC
01:41:22 KST

Starting in late summer 2026, a new MOKH module began to be detected in Russian Geran-class attack drones. This module is designed to improve the accuracy of autonomous navigation without the use of a satellite signal.
A representative of the Defence Intelligence of Ukraine (DIU) shared this information in a comment to Militarnyi.
According to him, the drone’s inertial navigation system has also changed with the introduction of the new module. Two additional sensors, located in the left and right wings, are connected to it. Together with the central module, they form a three-point measurement system that allows for more accurate determination of the drone’s motion parameters during autonomous flight.
“This creates a triangle—a measurable inertial environment—that allows for greater accuracy in autonomous navigation without satellite navigation,” explained the DIU representative.
According to him, even if other guidance systems are jammed, the drone will still be able to continue its flight to the designated area.
Accuracy in this mode will be lower, but the system should allow the drone to remain capable of striking targets without a stable satellite signal.
In this way, Russian developers are attempting to reduce the strike drones’ dependence on external navigation systems, which can be jammed by electronic warfare measures.
The Defence Intelligence of Ukraine (DIU) also notes that the overall trend regarding the use of foreign electronic components in Russian weaponry has not changed significantly.
In cruise and ballistic missiles, as well as in some attack drones, U.S.-manufactured components continue to account for the largest share of the foreign electronics identified.
A DIU representative named Texas Instruments and Altera among the manufacturers.
Products from STMicroelectronics and Chinese manufacturers are also found in Russian weapons systems. In certain types of Russian weapons systems, notably the Garpiya and Filin, the proportion of Chinese components already predominates.
The DIU representative also reported that Russian manufacturers are increasingly physically destroying markings on foreign electronics even during the weapons production process.
According to him, this is done on a massive scale on the assembly line to make it more difficult to determine the true origin of the components.
China remains one of the main channels through which foreign electronics enter Russia, as it is home to major distributors of Western manufacturers. Once the components are resold to local companies, it becomes much more difficult to track their subsequent movement.

Slavi Trifonov Announces Closure of 7/8 TV After Seven Years
Bulgarian television channel 7/8 is shutting down after seven years of broadcasting because of what its owner Slavi Trifonov describes as a cartel controlling the country's television advertising market, he announced in a post on Facebook.
Trifonov, leader of the There Is Such a People (ITN) party, said the two major private national television networks had secured control over advertising revenue, leaving smaller independent broadcasters unable to compete. He did not name the networks explicitly, but implied that he was referring to bTV and Nova TV.
According to Trifonov, the larger broadcasters reserve advertising inventory in advance and require advertisers to place their commercials exclusively with them, regardless of audience size or viewer preferences. He argued that this practice violates competition and antitrust rules.
He said the 7/8 team had made a serious effort to operate under these conditions for seven years, but the structure of the advertising market had made the channel's continued existence impossible.
"In this specific case, a small private television channel cannot exist because the two major private national networks have formed a cartel - they snap up all the advertising inventory in advance and force advertisers to place ads exclusively with them," Trifonov wrote.
He argued that the television market was not operating according to free-market principles, adding that the advance purchase of advertising space was intended to exclude other broadcasters.
"Television channels rely on advertising revenue; when two entities buy up all the ad space in advance with the clear intent of shutting everyone else out, in violation of the law and anti-monopoly regulations, there is no room for free and independent television," he said.
Trifonov thanked the channel's colleagues, staff and viewers in his Facebook post.
"Life is a battle, and we shall meet again on the battlefield - because we are the bad guys!" he concluded.
TV 7/8 began broadcasting in November 2019. In early 2020, Trifonov and his team of scriptwriters founded the There Is Such a People party. The channel initially hoped viewers would pay an additional 78 stotinki on top of their subscription fees.
Trifonov became the nominal leader of a former parliamentary party whose support fell below 1% in the most recent snap parliamentary elections.

Dealers of Hate: Kyiv Independent documentary investigates aggression against Ukrainians in Europe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:34:21 UTC
01:34:21 KST

Dealers of Hate: Kyiv Independent documentary investigates aggression against Ukrainians in Europe
The Kyiv Independent has released "Dealer of Hate," a new documentary by investigative reporter Danylo Mokryk that examines aggression against Ukrainians in the EU countries that took in the largest number of refugees following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The documentary premiered on Oct. 30 online on the Kyiv Independent YouTube channel and at an in-person screening in Kyiv, followed by a discussion with the team behind the film.
The film traces how hate speech on social media and from the political stage feeds hostility toward Ukrainians — and how that hostility turns into real-world aggression on the streets of German, Czech and Polish cities.
It shows that anti-Ukrainian sentiment has been actively fueled by local politicians, including Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla in Germany, Tomio Okamura and Andrej Babis in the Czech Republic, and Grzegorz Braun and Karol Nawrocki in Poland. Surges have been especially intense during election campaigns.
At the center of the film are Ukrainian women who have faced everyday aggression, physical assault, and a sense of being left unprotected by the police. Their experiences are only a few among many, as hundreds of Ukrainians in the three countries have become victims of anti-Ukrainian sentiment.
“I first started floating the idea to investigate anti-Ukrainian movements in the EU countries back in 2023, when our War Crimes Investigations Unit had just been created,” Mokryk said. “Since then, those movements have grown stronger, European politicians exploiting anti-Ukrainian narratives have grown more popular — and, most importantly, the attacks on Ukrainian refugees in the EU countries have considerably grown in numbers.
“Instrumentalizing hate is dangerous. And we wanted to show a strong connection between words of hate and real physical attacks. Of course, freedom of speech is important. But it comes with responsibility. And this is what our new documentary is really about: responsibility.”
The documentary draws on the Kyiv Independent's own analysis of tens of thousands of posts about Ukrainians on X in Czech, Polish and German, carried out together with data analyst Denys Hubashov. Using an AI model, the team identified the most widespread anti-Ukrainian narratives in each country and examined how they resonate with local populations.
"Dealers of Hate" is also available in Ukrainian on the YouTube channel of the Kyiv Independent's media partner Ukrainska Pravda.
Readers who want to support further investigations like this one can join the Kyiv Independent community.

Pontiff calls for institutions to put ethical principles into practice in guiding AI development
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:31:13 UTC
01:31:13 KST

Burak Bir
30 October 2026•Update: 30 October 2026
Pope Leo said Friday that institutions are needed to put ethical principles into practice to guide the development of artificial intelligence, stressing that AI must serve the common good and that certain decisions should never be delegated to machines.
Speaking at a gathering in the Vatican on the future of AI, the pope stressed the importance of keeping the human person at the heart of this technology to avoid the danger of threatening the common good and reducing people to data points.
Nevertheless, "you share a certain sense of unease regarding the development of artificial intelligence. We recognize the direction we should take, yet not enough is being done to move forward," the pontiff was quoted as saying by Vatican News.
"The future of AI is not pre-determined; machines are tools, not people; certain decisions cannot ever be delegated; intelligent technologies must be directed to the common good," he noted, underlining: "Institutions are needed to put ethical principles into practice to guide AI development."
The pope said that since human beings develop AI, its future relies on the choices humanity makes. He noted that this is why "we have the responsibility to guide, change, and, when necessary, reject its applications.."
"The question is not just, ‘What can AI do?’ Instead, it needs to be, ‘What purpose should it serve?’” said the pontiff.

Andreas Malm says UK travel ban shows 'noone is safe anymore'
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:31:04 UTC
01:31:04 KST

Breadcrumb
Andreas Malm says UK travel ban ahead of Palestine event shows 'noone is safe anymore'
Swedish academic Andreas Malm fears he may never be able to travel to the United Kingdom, a place he called his "academic home", after being denied entry on Wednesday in a move described as an attempt to curb academic freedom.
The professor, known for his book The Destruction of Palestine Is The Destruction of the Earth, was set to speak at an event organised by The Tribune alongside Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori to discuss the state of the American Empire today and Britain's role in it, and repression against the Palestine solidarity movement in Britain.
The Home Office cancelled Malm's Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) by email, saying that his presence in the UK is "not considered to be conducive to the public good". The New Arab reached out to the Home Office for comment, though it said it does not routinely comment on individual cases.
"I'm blocked from a country that I've been used to going to for a very long time, and that means a lot to me personally," Andreas Malm told The New Arab.
"This tells you something about where we are in 2026 when they go after someone like me, who you would normally consider to be a privileged, sheltered and protected person, who has a passport and can travel freely, but apparently not."
"No one is safe anymore, and it's not going to end with me. I'm just a small little station along this journey towards authoritarianism."
Malm stressed that he had frequently travelled to the United Kingdom, having lectured at prestigious institutions including Oxford and Cambridge, and that his previous work on climate politics and Palestine had never prevented him from travelling to the country and exchanging ideas.
"I had a fantastic period of about a week in the UK in May with my seven-year-old son, and ever since then has been just asking to go back to London to all the museums, now it's probably the last time that I was there," Malm said.
The academic stressed that his ban is nothing compared to what his friends in Gaza are going through as Israel's genocidal war rages on.
Oliver Eagleton, editor of The Tribune, described the ban on Malm as part of a worrying trend.
"It shouldn't be one of surprise because we've already seen the exact same ban put on Hassan Piker coming into the country earlier in the summer," Malm told The New Arab.
Piker and his uncle, Cenk Uygur, were denied entry in June on the same grounds when they were due to speak at SXSW London and the Oxford Union.
Eagleton said he assumed there would be more respect for academic freedom, particularly given the Burnham government's attempt to distance itself from the positions held by the previous administration of Keir Starmer's.
"I thought because of that these kinds of attacks on Palestine solidarity might ease up a bit just to not cause problems for the Burnham optics," Eagleton said.
"I was very surprised then to see that this is actually not just a continuation of what was happening before, but actually an escalation bringing those restrictions on freedom of expression into the realm of scholarship and academia."
While it is unclear why Malm was banned and given no option to appeal, he said he can only assume it was because he was due to attend the event alongside one of the co-founders of banned group Palestine Action.
"I'm guilty by association here only by dint of having a planned conversation with her, which is insane because she's not under arrest, she's not convicted of anything," Malm said. "If I'm considered some kind of threat to the public good just by talking to her, does that mean that people who talk to me are also a threat to the public good?"
"It's total absurdity. Where does this end? Where does this chain of guilt by association end if it's on this basis?"
Leading figures across politics, the arts, and academia, including author Sally Rooney and Labour MPs Clive Lewis and John McDonnell, have spoken out in support of Malm.
The professor will now appear at the event online, with the publication planning to include contributions from others on the state of free speech and academic freedom in Britain today.
"Although the government would like to stamp out events like this entirely, we will refuse to submit to that, and he will be free to present his arguments and ideas, and they're certain to travel much more widely now that the government has given him all this publicity," Eagleton said.
Malm said the ban is part of the "general wrongness" of the genocide in Gaza.
"This is part of the moment of the genocide in Palestine. This is part of the moment of climate breakdown. This is totally out of control," Malm said.
"It is part of the moment of the AI monster growing to eat us all. It's a general situation of drift towards disaster and this fascisisation that is happening in Britain and other countries, just one part of it."

Atelier Zébulon Perron draws on metabolist influence for Montreal bistro
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:30:00 UTC
01:30:00 KST

Atelier Zébulon Perron draws on metabolist influence for Montreal bistro
A monochrome palette and influences from Japanese metabolism characterise Bistrot à Franky in Montreal, Canada designed by local outfit Atelier Zébulon Perron.
The restaurant is a home base for local chef Francis Blais in the city’s hip Mile End neighbourhood.
Atelier Zébulon Perron took what it views as the standard design language of a Montreal bistro – bright lighting and lots of activity – and translated it into a more contemporary design.
For studio founder Zebulon Perron, the monochrome whites and beiges, interspersed with milled aluminium accents and a large zinc bar top, allowed the studio to experiment with textures and lighting to create visual interest and contrast in the dining space.
“With the monochromy of the restaurant, we experimented with textures – shiny versus matte, tile nd and stucco – and how light reacts to those surfaces in different ways,” Perron told Dezeen.
The studio emphasised the postmodern and “retrofuturist” elements of the design, pointing to the custom chandeliers with their illuminated Pyrex tubes and exposed wiring, fabricated by Perron’s long-time collaborators, local lighting design studio Lambert & Fils.
Perron highlighted the milled aluminium wine cellar that sits above the bar face, interspersed with portholes that are a direct reference to Japanese metabolist architecture.
“There’s a postmodern, 1980s aesthetic that naturally rose from everything we were doing,” said Perron.
Visitors enter the restaurant through a red-painted hallway and a metal door and handle carved from butcher block by local cabinetmaker Olivier Doray.
Inside, only the terrazzo floor was a holdover from the building’s former use. Granite tabletops cover some of the larger tables, while the classic bistrot white tablecloths are draped over the smaller tables.
Blond leather banquettes were placed below large mirrors on the wall opposite the bar, and these larger seating arrangements are centred by large butcher block tables, also fabricated by Doray.
Custom walnut chairs were designed by local industrial designer Guillaume Sasseville.
On the walls, white tile is interspersed with stucco and works of art, curated by local filmmaker Xavier Dolan. These artworks give pops of colour and Perron said that the monochromatic design elements allow both the food and the artworks to stand out in the space.
“Since the canvas is pretty neutral, the food and the artwork take centre stage,” he said.
A set of windows opens up the kitchen space to the dining room.
Custom bar seating features white columns with seats informed by transportation design, and Perron noted that the metal details and clean lines of the bar space, as well as the metal fans, also give the interior a streamlined look.
Atelier Zébulon Perron has designed some of the most interesting interior spaces in the city, including Café Constance and the dining areas for the city’s Four Seasons hotel.
It also helped create the pop-up bar staged during the city’s inaugural design week earlier this year.

Star Wars: Has Russia's war with Ukraine gone intergalactic?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:29:01 UTC
01:29:01 KST

Star Wars: Has Russia's war with Ukraine gone intergalactic?
Russian made an unprecedented combative move this month as one of its military satellites, the Cosmos-2612, encroached upon the orbit of Ukrainian commercial satellite, Iceye-X36, in behaviour deemed "threatening" by the US State Department. Norbert Pouzin, an orbital analyst at French space tech firm, Aldoria, described the mercenary manoeuvre as the first of its kind.
Has space become a new frontier in Russia's war with Ukraine?
Russian military satellite Cosmos-2612 carried out a manoeuvre between October 15 and 18 that brought it “dangerously close” to Ukrainian commercial satellite, Iceye-X36. The move was described by US Under Secretary of State for Arms Control and International Security as "threatening".
Operated by Finnish company Iceye, Iceye-X36 is a Finnish-American civilian satellite equipped with Synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) to provide satellite images to the Ukrainian Armed Forces.
The US State Department said Russia's tactic was consistent with “in-orbit military operations”.
Analysts specialising in space surveillance have been following Cosmos-2612 since its launch in April.
"Cosmos-2612 was one of six satellites launched in total. It was immediately apparent that this wasn't a classic deployment. As soon as they took off, the satellites started changing orbit to pursue Iceye satellites,” said Norbert Pouzin, an orbital analyst at Aldoria, a French space surveillance firm.
Cosmos-2612 took off on April 6, 2026 alongside Cosmos-2609, Cosmos-2610, Cosmos-2611, Cosmos-2613 and Cosmos-2614. KeepTrack, a site specialising in satellite navigation, enables viewers to track their paths.
Orbit re-routing – as has been the case of the Cosmos satellites – is a move that consumes a lot of fuel. It’s also the first step in approaching another satellite, Pouzin explains:
 "If two satellites are travelling in the same orbit, then they don’t need as much fuel to approach one another. Changing directions in space uses a lot of fuel. But once in the same orbit as another satellite, you’ve already executed the most costly move fuel-wise, if you then want to carry out an approach.”
From a kilometre to within just a few hundred metres
As the imaging data via site, Satellite Tracker, corroborates, Cosmos-2612 diverted from its original position – around 400-500 km from Iceye-X36 – to get closer to the Finnish-American satellite.
"On October 15, Cosmos-2612 was within 5 kilometres of Iceye-X36. Its position continued to narrow in on the satellite on October 16 and 17, before finally getting to within a few hundred metres and a kilometre of Iceye-X36 ,” Pouzin said.
Satellite imaging company Vantor published a photo of the two satellites on October 22, depicting their orbits withing just 1.02 kilometres of one another.
To display this content from X (Twitter), you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
Data from KeepTrack also revealed that Cosmos-2612 and Iceye-X36 later embarked on the same orbit, meaning the Russian satellite was “following” the Finnish-American satellite.
A bold move
So why did Cosmos-2612 carry out this “threatening” manoeuvre?
Given the lack of debris, it doesn’t appear that Iceye-X36 was the target of a “kinetic” attack – that is, a physical strike involving a collision or the launch of a projectile. But according to Pouzin, the manoeuvre by Cosmos-2612 could be interpreted as a form of exerting pressure on Ukraine, as it is the direct recipient of the data gathered by the Iceye satellite:
 "SAR satellites have unique observation plans [Editor’s note: a schedule that coordinates how radar satellites can scan specific parts of the planet.] If an operator knows about these, then he could – for a short time – disrupt the satellite’s mission, potentially causing repercussions for ground-based or maritime operations, for example."
Cosmos-2612’s move seemed to shock Western commentators, he added:
 "While Russia regularly launches military satellites in the same orbital planes as classified American military satellites; carrying out this particular kind of approach on a commercial satellite while in a low orbit is something new. Furthermore it seemed to be non-cooperative in nature: we are dealing with two actors who are not on the same side and these are satellites not operated by the same entity."
The initiative also revealed something about Russia’s capabilities, Pouzin concluded:
 "The move demonstrated a certain agility by the Russian operator, a skilled knowledge of the space domain, and a very high level of mastery in this type of navigation.”

’Tis the season to shop Ukrainian: Kyiv Independent launches 2026 Holiday Gift Guide
The Kyiv Independent has launched its 2026 Holiday Gift Guide, a curated selection of 80 items from Ukrainian brands and creators that showcase the country's creativity, craftsmanship, and cultural heritage.
The guide brings together recommendations from Kyiv Independent staff across the newsroom and beyond, featuring Ukrainian-made clothing, accessories, jewelry, home decor, books, self-care products, and more. From established fashion designers to independent artisans, the selection highlights the breadth of Ukrainian design and the people shaping it.
"You can’t tell Ukraine’s story without showcasing the country’s creativity and creators," said Liliane Bivings, business editor at the Kyiv Independent, who led the project.
"As a huge fan (and shopper!) of Ukrainian brands, I couldn’t be more excited to put these names in front of the world," she said.
The guide features brands that draw on Ukraine's history and traditions while reinterpreting them for contemporary audiences.
Gaptuvalnya embroidered shirt, for example, is inspired by traditional ornamentation, while Aqyar Ceramics' handmade stoneware reflects Crimean Tatar heritage. Other items offer a more modern take on Ukrainian identity, from minimalist jewelry and sculptural home decor to clothing designed for everyday wear. Pavuk, which teamed up with the Kyiv Independent on a limited-edition collaboration, revives the pavuk, a traditional straw mobile once woven to protect the home.
"Being featured in the Kyiv Independent’s holiday gift guide is a wonderful opportunity for us to introduce international audiences to Ukrainian culture and its heritage, to share our traditions and to show how they continue to live on and take new forms in the modern world," the brand said.
Anoeses, one of the brands featured in the guide, highlights the importance of introducing international audiences to the diversity of Ukrainian design.
"Being part of The Kyiv Independent’s selection is especially meaningful, as it’s an opportunity to introduce an international audience to the work of Ukrainian brands and show just how diverse Ukrainian design is," Anoeses said.
The selection also highlights the stories behind the products. A ceramic pendant by Ukrainian artist Viktoria Belyavska is made using some of the last clay sourced from Donbas before Russian troops advanced toward the deposit. The Ukrainian brand Jul, whose floral-print anorak is in our guide, lost part of its production and stock in a Russian attack outside of Kyiv in March, underscoring the challenges local businesses continue to face during the war.
Alongside Ukrainian creators and independent brands, the guide features merchandise from the Kyiv Independent store. This includes The Power Within, the newsroom’s first print magazine and a record of life in wartime Ukraine, as well as the Ancient Coins hoodie and beanie, the Trident Bird T-shirt, and the Borshch apron. Readers can also gift a Kyiv Independent membership, giving someone access to benefits such as reporter Q&As and Ukrainian language lessons.
More than a collection of gift ideas, the guide offers readers a way to discover Ukrainian creators and support businesses whose work reflects the country's cultural identity, ingenuity, and continued creative life during Russia's war.
The 2026 Holiday Gift Guide is available now on the Kyiv Independent website.
Editor's note: The guide is being published ahead of the holiday season to give readers time to browse, place orders, and account for international shipping. Delivery times may vary by brand and destination.

Police in Scotland launch Andrew and Epstein royal castle investigation
Media reports say the inquiries are related to claims that women were trafficked to the king’s Balmoral estate.
Police in Scotland have opened an investigation into the time the former Prince Andrew spent with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, at the king’s Balmoral estate.
Police Scotland, which provides law enforcement throughout the country, said on Friday that the inquiries began after it received “information” and that the investigation was at a “very early stage″.
The force provided no further detail about what the information was or what offences officers were investigating.
The investigation was first reported by The Daily Express, which said the inquiries were related to claims that women were trafficked to the king’s private estate in the Scottish Highlands.
“All inquiries are evidence-led, with the needs of victim survivors at the heart of those inquiries,″ Police Scotland said in a statement. “We would never confirm details of ongoing inquiries and it would be inappropriate to comment further.”
Scotland shooting holiday
Images released by the United States Department of Justice appeared to show Epstein and Maxwell on a shooting trip at Balmoral in 1999. The photos were among millions of pages of documents the department published earlier this year as Congress probed Epstein’s links to politicians, business leaders and other influential people in the US and around the world.
The presence of anyone’s name or image in the files is not proof of wrongdoing.
Several other UK police forces, including London’s Metropolitan Police Service, Thames Valley Police and Surrey Police, are also investigating information released in the Epstein Files.
In February, Thames Valley officers arrested the former prince, now known as Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, on suspicion of misconduct in public office, based on information uncovered in the trove of documents released by US authorities.
The 66-year-old younger brother of King Charles III was held for several hours before being released on police bail pending further investigation.
It was the first time in nearly four centuries that a senior British royal had been arrested.
The former prince has repeatedly denied committing any crimes.
Epstein links
Mountbatten-Windsor’s links to Epstein have caused headaches for Britain’s royal family for almost two decades.
With US authorities preparing to release documents related to their long-running investigation into Epstein, the king late last year moved to shield the monarchy from the scandal by stripping his brother of his princely title.
Mountbatten-Windsor was also ordered to move out of the Royal Lodge, his longtime home in parkland near Windsor Castle. He now lives in a house at Sandringham, the king’s privately owned estate in eastern England.
The former prince’s reputation has been tarnished by his relationship with Epstein ever since 2008, when the wealthy American financier pleaded guilty to soliciting a minor for prostitution. In 2011, the late Virginia Giuffre alleged that she had been trafficked by Epstein and forced to have sex with Mountbatten-Windsor when she was 17.
Mountbatten-Windsor tried to silence the scandal by giving a lengthy interview to the BBC in 2019, but the strategy backfired when he was criticised for offering unbelievable explanations of his behaviour and failing to show empathy for Epstein’s victims.

The world’s biggest cities are sinking. Is yours one of them?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:26:10 UTC
01:26:10 KST

Major cities across the world—including hotspots such as New Orleans, Mexico City, Jakarta and Rome—are sinking by up to several inches every year.
Those are the findings of an exhaustive new survey published in Nature Cities, in which researchers used satellite radar to track 465 urban areas of more than a million people from 2014 to 2023. The results, displayed in an interactive map, shows that sinking isn’t just “a local curiosity” for a small handful of cities, but “a global urban problem,” says study coauthor Guoquan Wang, a geophysicist at the University of Houston.
Satellites can measure the land’s gradual sinking, called subsidence, by taking radar images of the same area over time to determine the shift in the radar signal’s travel—even a change of mere millimeters (twenty-fifths of an inch) of ground can result in a signal taking slightly longer to return than the past. The new work, which examined small chunks of land—just a few houses wide—all over the world, is “the most comprehensive and systematic exploration of subsidence in urban cities,” says Roland Bürgmann, a geophysicist at the University of California, Berkeley, who was not involved in the study.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Sinking was most severe in Southeast Asia, West and Central Asia and North America, but it also turned up in South America and Africa, both of which are generally less studied in regards to land subsidence; For almost half the cities in the dataset, no satellite radar study had ever been done before.
Different factors can contribute to urban subsidence. In New York City, for instance, the weight of buildings compresses the region’s soft soils. But the biggest driver is usually water utilities, industries and other groups pumping out water from under the ground. Groundwater helps hold up the soil like air in a cushion: pump it out, and the ground slowly sags.
And the real danger is uneven sinking. “If the whole city were to smoothly subside altogether by an inch or so, it wouldn’t be that big of a problem,” Bürgmann says. But when one neighborhood drops faster than the next, the strain builds.
Over time such strain can crack foundations, break sewer lines, damage subway systems and worsen flooding. In Jakarta, the sinking and flooding has become so severe that Indonesia is building a brand-new capital city on the island of Borneo.
Once it happens, sinking is “cumulative and largely irreversible,” Wang says, but cities have successfully stopped continued subsidence before. Tokyo once sank “way faster than many cities today,” says Manoochehr Shirzaei, a geoscientist at Virginia Tech, who was a peer reviewer for the study, until officials drew up policies to halt it. These included regulations around groundwater pumping and a shift toward alternative surface water sources. In China, Beijing and the nearby city of Tianjin “stopped pumping groundwater and replaced it with surface water” piped from the Yangtze River basin, Wang says, and sinking has since halted in parts of the region.
“In most places, we have plenty of time to react,” Shirzaei says, “but we have to do it.”

This October is on track to be the hottest ever recorded
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:26:07 UTC
01:26:07 KST

This October is almost certainly going to be the hottest October ever recorded. Global temperatures this month are set to be around 1.76 degrees Celsius (about 3.17 degrees Fahrenheit) above preindustrial levels, surpassing the previous record set in 2023, researchers predict.
An especially hot October also puts 2026 on track to be among the hottest years ever recorded—if not the hottest—according to projections from climate scientists Andrew Dessler and Zeke Hausfather. Their projection is based on data collected by the Europe-based Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S).
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Next year could be even more blistering. “This year’s record-setting October is a sign that the ‘Super El Niño’ is kicking into gear and will likely be the first in a series of record-setting months, culminating in a record-setting 2027,” Hausfather says.
El Niño is a cyclic climate pattern that occurs when part of the Pacific Ocean is unusually warm, affecting weather across the world. El Niño can exacerbate climate change—which is driven by the burning of fossil fuels—to boost global temperatures.
In 2023, also an El Niño year, October temperatures reached 1.7 degrees C (3.06 degrees F) above preindustrial levels, according to Dessler and Hausfather’s analysis. The year was the hottest ever recorded at the time, after which it was surpassed by 2024. The following year, 2025, was the third-hottest year ever recorded.
October’s likely record follows several other superlative moments so far in 2026, including the U.S.’s hottest September, hottest first eight months and hottest 12-month period ever recorded, as well as the hottest global ocean temperatures ever recorded.

John Turturro Will Pick Your Pocket and Steal Your Heart
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:26:04 UTC
01:26:04 KST

If it seems like no one else could play the role John Turturro plays in The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, you can imagine the angst writer-director Noah Segan felt when he sent the screenplay to the actor hoping for a “yes.” Turturro brings world-weariness, tenderness, and New York City street smarts to his turn as Harry, a career criminal whose way of life is disappearing in a cashless, electronic, often colder world. The character may steal to put food on his table, but he’s also loyal and honest in his own way, caring for a permanently disabled wife and practically a saint when compared with the tech-enabled, mafia nepo baby (Will Price) he makes the mistake of stealing from, setting off the movie’s drama and putting his life in jeopardy.
Turturro, who has been a ubiquitous presence in film, TV, and theater for decades, truly seems to be everywhere these days—in an acclaimed production heading for Broadway, in Severance, whose fans eagerly await a third season, in the forthcoming climate-change dramedy A Statement from Spotlight director Tom McCarthy, and of course anywhere the Knicks are. With Pickpocket, he could very well land his first Oscar nomination in a career full of performances that have certainly qualified for consideration, from Barton Fink to Quiz Show to more Spike Lee films than any other actor has appeared in.
Ahead of the theatrical release of The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, which hit theaters nationwide on Oct. 30, Turturro spoke to TIME about how his hometown has changed, his love for collaborators old and new, and his nerves heading into this year’s NBA season.
Noah Segan said that when he came to meet you, “We had some soup and fell in love.” Did you need to be convinced to take the part?
I read so many scripts, and so many of them are derivative. Sometimes they're just violent for violence's sake. Someone's seen you do something, and they say, "Well, he could do this.” I said, "Is this as good as I think it is?” I was struck by the structure of it, because I love Greek plays. I love that Aristotelian 24-hour time frame, when something has tension and propulsive movement, an odyssey to survive in a short time, and then it's juxtaposed with this tenderness and the specificity of language. I met Noah, and I liked him. He's a gentle guy, but he has a backbone. When Noah gave me the script, it's like a gift. You want to reciprocate. You want to surprise that person.
Harry is a criminal, but he operates by a code. He’s true to his word. He’s loyal to his wife. Do you see him as an antihero?
I just try to play a person. I’ve read about a lot of these guys. They were from broken homes, orphanages. They didn’t have a family, so they formed this little family with other people who didn’t want to hurt people. Even though it is a violation, it was nonviolent. It was like a magic trick. They’re taking something. But there’s a lot of people who pick our pockets every day. And they take our world sometimes.
The movie has a real nostalgia for the old New York, a more analog time. Do you share that feeling?
Everything changes. You walk down Bleecker Street, all these theaters, nightclubs are gone. It’s CVS. Ethnic neighborhoods aren’t there anymore. It takes away from the texture of a neighborhood. The thing I miss is things being affordable. When I was young, even if I sat in the back, I could see anyone. Jimi Hendrix at the Electric Circus. Colleen Dewhurst or George C. Scott. I got an education that way, while I was getting a [formal] education, and it opened up my horizons of thinking someday I could make a living doing this.
The city also feels different from decades past because we’re all staring down at our phones instead of looking at each other as we walk down the street.
There's so many people. We're all going somewhere. And there's plenty of people that aren't there. There's a lot of people gone now from all different generations, and you're more and more surrounded by ghosts. In my phone, I don't take people out because maybe I need the number in the afterlife or something. You just understand that there is a clock to our lives, and what you give is also important. It's not just what you take, and I believe in that.
The movie was filmed in every borough, right? It doesn’t feel like a gimmick, but something that could plausibly happen in this character’s life.
The guy is sort of a superhero. He knows the transit lines, the buses, the subways. He doesn't take Ubers. I take subways and I walk everywhere. I love it when I go to an event and everyone's sharing that on the train. It’s kind of about the underbelly, the people keep the city humming. Even though this is not a film about the working class, it is, sort of. The elevator doesn't work. The heat isn't so great. These are real problems, and those people sometimes are not explored as much.
There’s a wonderful scene where Harry dances to the song “Native New Yorker” for his wife Rosie, who is disabled and non-verbal. Was that improvised?
I like to dance. I studied dance. In my household, everybody was dancing, three boys, my mom was a great dancer. I used to go out dancing to that song. When people are incapacitated, you play music, you sing, you dance. It’s a love scene. Movement, especially when it’s not overly choreographed, brings joy. Even in intense stories, people stop to do things. They stop to eat. They stop to have a laugh.
You go way back with two of your co-stars, Giancarlo Esposito, who plays a detective who’s almost like a colleague of Harry’s, and Steve Buscemi, who owns the pawn shop where he brings his stolen wares. How did that come about? Did you suggest them?
Yeah, we talked about it, and I asked Giancarlo to read it. And Steve and I know each other. We've been neighbors. He's a beautiful guy. He's a beautiful actor. We have a history there, so it's not like we have to invent that. So that was helpful in the movie.
You and Tatiana Maslany, who’s also in this film, just finished the play Rhinoceros together. Do you like to get back to the theater every once in a while to sort of sharpen the tools?
That’s where I come from. I love the rehearsal process, if it’s a very open one, which we did in Rhinoceros with [director] Diane Paulus. We explored everything. It’s exhausting, I don’t want to do a run for half a year. But I love doing things that young people can come to and afford. It’s real teamwork, and I think it’s kept me fresh for doing film work. It’s humbling, and it’s nerve-racking, and it’s also exhilarating when you’re able to keep your balance.
There’s so much love for your character Irving on Severance. And fans really obsess over this show with conspiracy theories. Have you been a part of something like that before?
I love Irving too. I have enjoyed working with the entire group, and especially with the apple of my eye, Chris [Walken]. Severance poses questions of work life, personal life. Maybe it resonates in the world. Maybe even more now with all this AI stuff. I think one of the strengths of the show is that it poses these questions and doesn’t answer them. When you answer it, it’s not as satisfying as figuring it out.
As a prominent Knicks fan, how are you feeling about this season?
I feel hopeful. I’m not overconfident. It was beautiful how they all coalesced. I treasure being a fan and a season-ticket holder. I’m still soaking it all in. My favorite thing was coming home on the train, everyone just being in shock. It’s great when people come together.
Correction, Oct. 30
The original version of this story misstated which season of Severance is forthcoming. It will be the third season, not the fourth.

Russia’s human rights commissioner says humanitarian mission in occupied Oleshky is wrapping up
Russia’s human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, said the humanitarian mission in the city of Oleshky is coming to an end.
“We are finishing our humanitarian mission in Oleshky. We’re already in Armiansk now. We’re getting people seated into the convoys [of buses],” Lantratova said.
The convoy carrying Oleshky residents who chose to evacuate is headed to Russia and Ukraine, she said. Davyd Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People faction in the Verkhovna Rada, said earlier that the Ukrainian delegation, along with some of those evacuated from Oleshky, traveled to Anapa and is expected to fly from there to Belarus and then on to Ukraine.
Lantratova said the humanitarian mission went off “without any incidents”:
Thanks to our troops, who made all of this possible. A huge convoy: 25 buses, nine ambulances, buses for bedridden people. We managed to do everything. I thank the first lady [of the U.S., Melania Trump], and I thank everyone who took part in this effort.
The city of Oleshky sits in the part of the Kherson region occupied by Russian forces, where the war has caused a humanitarian catastrophe.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to halt fighting in Oleshky for the humanitarian mission, with U.S. first lady Melania Trump mediating.
The truce began on the morning of October 27 and will remain in effect until late in the evening of November 1. Neither side has reported any violations. Arakhamia called the truce in Oleshky “the biggest de-escalation since 2022.”

Trump, Obama serve up a food fight in final days of midterm campaign
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:21:34 UTC
01:21:34 KST

Trump, Obama serve up a food fight in final days of midterm campaign
WASHINGTON, Oct 30 - Former President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump are having a food fight in the closing days of the midterm election campaign, trading barbs over the Cheesecake Factory as voters prepare to decide control of Congress.
Obama struck a nerve with Trump by mocking his gold-heavy White House renovations, saying during an October 24 campaign stop in Ohio that the president had the place “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory." Trump clapped back at Obama this week with lengthy defenses of both his renovations and the restaurant chain.
The restaurant flap is the latest offbeat detour in a campaign in which Trump has warned darkly about communism, commented on the physique of men's bodies and joked that the $5,000 payments he is promising Americans if Republicans keep Congress would barely cover a meal at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.
Both men are trying to portray the other party as disconnected from voters' economic anxieties as Americans struggle with high prices, a central issue heading into Tuesday's election.
Campaigning for Democrats in Morrow, Georgia, on Wednesday, Obama said Trump and his followers were focusing on his Cheesecake Factory remarks instead of on inflation "and hope that you won't notice your bills are higher and your life is tougher."
“They mobilized a whole-of-government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke," Obama said. "They don't have solutions to actual problems, so they'd rather have the media and you talking about the Cheesecake Factory."
Responding to conservative critics who suggested his joke mocked patrons of the restaurant chain, Obama said: "I am the father of two daughters. Do you think I could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?"
Trump, never one to let a personal jibe go unanswered, seized on Obama's remarks during campaign stops in Texas and Mississippi.
"Every piece of lettuce he eats has to be perfect, and I'm not that choosy," Trump said in Corpus Christi, Texas, waving his arms around as if in the shape of a lettuce leaf.
Trump accused Obama of being elitist for mocking the restaurant chain, known for its multi-paged menu and an eclectic decor that can include Egyptian-style columns and palm trees, and dismissed complaints about his White House renovations.
“For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president,” Trump taunted Obama in comments to reporters on Monday.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined the fray on Tuesday, eating a French dip cheeseburger at the Cheesecake Factory in Washington and saying "the Martha's Vineyard set" should give the chain a try. Obama owns a home on the upscale Massachusetts island.
The episode is the latest flare-up in a rivalry that stretches back to 2011, when Trump gained political prominence by falsely accusing Obama of not being born in the US and Obama later mocked him in remarks at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner.
During this year's midterm campaign, Democrats have accused Trump of being out of touch with everyday Americans' concerns, while Trump has repeatedly played down higher gas prices since the war with Iran began.
Trump provided his opponents another opening this week when he talked in Texas about how people should spend the $5,000 checks he has proposed sending to Americans if Republicans retain control of Congress.
“You could even come to Mar-a-Lago," Trump said. "The problem is that for $5,000 the most you’ll be able to buy is a hamburger and maybe a small dessert.” REUTERS

US delays the Patriot missiles Ukraine needs against ballistic strikes but keeps sending older PAC-2s

The US is delaying PAC-3 interceptors for Ukraine’s Patriot air defense systems while older PAC-2s keep arriving, a NATO source told Radio Svoboda on 29 October. PAC-3 is the Patriot missile built mainly to stop ballistic missiles.
The delay comes as Russia leans on ballistic missiles against the capital. In two weeks, Russia launched more than 100 at Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in his 27 October evening address. “And above all, we do not have enough missiles for Patriots,” he added. On 29 October, Zelenskyy said Ukraine has intelligence that Russia is preparing new ballistic missile attacks. Kyiv is “awaiting the relevant decisions” on interceptor packages, “primarily for Patriots,” he said.
A question for politicians
The PAC-2s, used mostly against aircraft and cruise missiles, arrive through PURL, the NATO mechanism under which allies pay for US weapons for Ukraine. The PAC-3 delay is under discussion at a high political level, the NATO source said. It is unclear when the situation will change.
What Washington said before
On 20 October, Hegseth said in Wisconsin: “We haven’t changed our posture in any way toward the Ukrainians, but certainly with things like interceptors, we want to make sure our guys have the most possible as well.”

Uttarakhand chopper flying: A lot has changed for better, but a lot remains to be done
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:20:42 UTC
01:20:42 KST

NEW DELHI: Hours after seven people on board an Aryan Aviation chopper died when it crashed near Gaurikund on June 15, 2025, the aviation ministry had found two helicopters of Trans Bharat — whose chopper crashed on Friday — were airborne “under unsuitable weather conditions.” It had suspended the licences of both Trans Bharat pilots for six months.While the cause of Trans Bharat’s Friday crash in which six people lost their lives will be known once the inquiry report is out, there have been red flags regarding this and several other chopper operators in the hill region. The Uttarakhand govt has grounded Trans Bharat fleet for now.Aviation industry insiders point out that six days before Friday crash, another Trans Bharat helicopter carrying five pilgrims from Sahastradhara to Kedarnath via Guptkashi had made an emergency landing at Baurari stadium on Oct 24 “where children were playing.” Luckily all six, five passengers and the pilot, were safe that day and the chopper took off soon again.“On May 20, 2026, a Trans Bharat Bell 407 flying from Badrinath to Dehradun with seven people on board ran into severe downdrafts over the Chamba–Arakot sector of Tehri Garhwal. During the emergency landing that followed, its tail struck a 33 kV high-tension line. The pilot, a former IAF pilot, got everyone down uninjured,” said sources.
Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) is probing this case.The Char Dham corridor has no single agency answerable for safety. While the DGCA licenses the operators and pilots, UCADA runs the helipads, sets slots and manages shuttle operations. The Sanjay Kumar Jha-headed parliamentary standing committee on transport, tourism and culture had in Aug 2025 called this arrangement “inherently unsafe and unsustainable.” It said there was a “responsibility vacuum” between the two agencies. It found that the DGCA was acting as a passive licensing authority. It also noted that India still has no mandatory, terrain-specific mountain-flying training or certification for pilots operating in the Himalaya.This changed significantly after last summer following a spate of chopper crashes in Uttarakhand. Air traffic control units are being set up, with Kedarnath having one now and Badrinath to get a unti soon. Routes have been defined in the region and take offs are both restricted in number and controlled in a defined pattern with some gap. This is a far cry from the almost unregulated chopper movement in the hill region till last summer.“System wise there has been a lot of improvement. The Char Dham Operations are quite extensive in every aspect. From commercial to maintenance and from operations to ATC, every department is working very hard to ensure safety and efficiency is achieved. After the season of 2025 , there are many different measures that are implemented to ensure highest safety standards are met. These include ATC at Sahastradhara and Sitapur to ensure that flying is well coordinated and controlled,” said Captain Nitin Welde, a senior chopper pilot who operates in Uttarakhand.
“There’s a fuel bowser at Sahastradhara to ensure that IOCL supplies fuel in best possible manner. Take off and landing tarmac is separated from parking Tarmac to ensure orderly flow of positioning. There are CCTV cameras all across valley which give feed through a mobile app. All can get a live feed as regards weather valley. For higher helipads above 10,000 feet, the weight limitations are in place and that ensures higher reserve of power while landing and take off. Training for pilots has increased since last year. And there is adequate training in Char Dham sector as well as Kedar shuttles. The DGCA FOIs have been visiting the valley on a weekly basis and UCADA ops department is fully involved in a minute to minute monitoring and support,” added Captain Welde.

Poundland in peril: how rampant inflation and price wars left £1 stores exposed
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:20:41 UTC
01:20:41 KST

‘It was a very successful and simple proposition,” laments one former Poundland boss. With every product in the shop sold at £1, and the price in its name, its proposition to shoppers was the clearest of any UK high street chain.
Now the UK’s first and biggest nationwide single-price retailer could disappear amid heavy competition and inflation that has eaten into its ability to offer bargains.
Its potential collapse has brought distress for its up to 12,000 staff in the run-up to Christmas, and as shoppers head to the chain for Halloween costumes and treats.
Meanwhile, its low-profile owners are facing questions from the prime minister over their behaviour in the week his government’s budget attempted to offer support to the high street.
Poundland’s future hangs in the balance – and not for the first time – after the 36-year-old retailer filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the high court on Thursday, with the advisory firm AlixPartners lined up to run the process.
The legal measure protects Poundland, which operates 600 stores, including Dealz outlets in Ireland, from the demands of creditors for 10 days while a solution to its problems is sought. However, the prospect of it avoiding mass store closures and job losses diminishes by the day as suppliers hold back on deliveries, hurting its ability to trade.
The chain’s potential demise comes after Gordon Brothers, the American restructuring specialist which bought Poundland for a nominal £1 from its previous owner in June last year, rejected a management-backed rescue bid for the whole chain by Martin Property Group.
While the Northern Irish firm is still in talks about taking on Poundland, it is understood its offer amounts to about £15m. That would pay off only half the £30m shareholder loan, the majority of which was taken on by Gordon Brothers when it bought the company. The deal would also include taking on a further, asset-backed loan worth about £90m, it is understood.
This deal has been rejected by Gordon Brothers despite Pepco, Poundland’s former owner, which holds the other £7.5m of the debt, being prepared to wait for repayment in the hope of saving the business, as first reported by Sky News.
One source who knows Poundland well said that Gordon Brothers had already taken about £10m in fees and interest out of the chain in the last year and that wanting another £30m was “egregious”. Gordon Brothers did not respond to a request for comment and has not confirmed this figure.
Gordon Brothers said earlier this week that options for the whole and parts of the business “are being thoroughly and objectively evaluated, with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland’s people and all relevant stakeholders”.
Sources close to the process said Gordon Brothers was unwilling to accept the Martin deal as the latest offer includes only about £7.5m up front and the rest over the next two years, leaving uncertainty for creditors, staff and suppliers.
One source said Gordon Brothers had sought bidders for the whole of Poundland but “the market had spoken” and only one little-known financial bidder with no history of running a large retail chain in the UK had come forward who might only go on to break up Poundland itself.
Instead, the restructuring specialist is understood to believe that suppliers and staff would be safer with the “trusted established retail operators” who have already put forward firm offers for parcels of outlets that amount to about half of Poundland’s stores, which could be converted to their formats.
A deal may yet be agreed with Martin over the next 10 days, especially with political pressure from Andy Burnham. On Friday, he told the Telegraph: “We want to see jobs protected. If there was a potential owner to avoid this that hasn’t been accepted, then the business secretary and I want to know why that is the case.”
For now, Gordon Brothers appears more keen on a break-up after losing faith in the likelihood of Poundland finding a route to long-term profitability amid tough times on the high street and heavy competition.
Rapid inflation on the cost of goods and labour, energy and business rates in recent years has forced Poundland to take a hit on profits and sell products for more than £1, including items for £5 or more.
In the past, Poundland removed products if it could not sell them profitably for a pound, but its choices have become more limited. High inflation – triggered first by Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and then the Middle East conflict – has exposed a business model which always appeared to have a shelf life.
In most supermarkets a two-litre bottle of milk costs over £2, a pack of KitKats is at least £1.50 and a tin of Heinz baked beans is about £1.40, according to the price comparison site Trolley. Cutting the size of Poundland has, meanwhile, reduced its scale, making it harder to get good deals from suppliers to protect margins.
Poundland has also admitted that it made mistakes in recent years, including putting its Pepco clothing ranges into stores, which proved unpopular with UK shoppers.
The expansion of cut-price chains such as Savers, The Range, B&M, The Works and Home Bargains alongside budget online rivals such as Temu, Shein and Amazon means the cheaper end of the UK retail market is now very crowded.
Meanwhile, the low-wage shoppers that make up the core of Poundland’s clientele have little spare cash for non-essentials amid rising household bills. Those with more to spare have more options in their supermarket shop, where they are increasingly locked in by loyalty-card-linked discounts.
Poundland’s pre-tax losses widened to £85.3m in the year to September 2025, from a loss of £45.4m in 2024, as sales at its outlets in the UK, Republic of Ireland and Isle of Man slid almost 12% to £1.55bn, according to accounts filed at Companies House.
In September Poundland said its revenues had returned to growth, up 3.3% at established stores in the latest three-month period, but sources said the business was not generating enough cash to pay off its loans.
US-headquartered Gordon Brothers has a long history of involvement in selling off the assets of UK high street businesses, including offloading the stock and and fittings of failed retailers such as Toys R Us.
It previously owned the British fashion brands Laura Ashley and Ben Sherman, where it oversaw the closure of their stores, and it recently bought LK Bennett, which has also closed its stores this year.
One advisory expert said Poundland’s owners had intended the buyout to be a rescue operation rather than a break-up but ultimately: “Gordon Brothers has ended up doing what Gordon Brothers do. Leopards do not change their spots.”
He said Gordon Brothers was likely to “come out looking like the worst version” of a restructuring firm. The number of stores likely not to find an immediate buyer “might not be as catastrophic as half” but it was unlikely buyers would be found for all, he added.
Poundland’s possible demise is part of a wave of consolidation of similar outlets over the past decade.
Poundworld closed its 350 stores in 2018, and Poundland bought its rival 99p Stores in 2015. Poundland then closed about 200 of its then 800 UK stores in a restructuring last year.
Poundstretcher was bought by Majestic Wine’s owner, Fortress, in 2024.
Poundland itself has a rocky history during which it has passed in and out of the hands of investment firms. Founded with one store in Burton upon Trent in 1990, the company was listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2014 at a value of about £750m by its then owner, the buyout firm Warburg Pincus.
Just two years later, Poundland agreed to a £597m takeover by Steinhoff, the South African retail conglomerate, after the British chain struggled to digest the takeover of 99p stores.
By 2018, Poundland had to seek new investment after an accounting scandal at Steinhoff and was hived off into Pepco, a company formed from Steinhoff’s European retail business. Poundland was then preparing to rejoin the London stock market when the Covid pandemic hit in 2020, scotching those plans as high streets across the UK closed down for months.
Last year, with costs rising, Pepco was looking to sell. Gordon Brothers stepped in, snapping up the struggling chain with its £1 deal. It remains unclear whether someone new will flip another coin to bet on turning Poundland around.

European Commission proposes disbursing remaining EUR 45 bln from EUR 90 bln loan to Ukraine in 2027
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
18:19:50 EET
01:19:50 KST

The European Commission is proposing that the EU Council approve the disbursement to Ukraine of the remaining portion of the 2027 loan, amounting to EUR 45 billion, as part of the total financial support for the 2026-2027 period totalling EUR 90 billion.
The European Commission's press service announced the decision on Friday.
"Today, the European Commission took another step in the implementation of the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan, which will provide Ukraine with essential budgetary support and defence products in 2026 and 2027. The package adopted today includes a proposal for the Council to approve the remaining loan amount of €45 billion for 2027," the statement reads.
Commenting on the decision, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said: "With today's proposal, we are providing Ukraine with much-needed predictability and helping maintain essential public services."
According to her, strengthening support for Ukraine is "high on the agenda in Montreal" [where the EU-Canada summit is taking place]. "Together with our allies, we must also do everything in our power to mount pressure on Russia to stop its barbaric war of aggression," von der Leyen added.
In addition, it is reported that after the European Commission issued a positive assessment of the Financing Strategy submitted by Ukraine on October 26, 2026, a proposal for a Council implementing decision was also adopted. "[This document] sets out the provision of the remaining €45 billion to Ukraine by 31 December 2027. The support will be allocated to: the budget support, reaching up to €13.3 billion and split equally between the Ukraine Facility and Macro-Financial Assistance, and Ukraine's defence industrial capacity, accounting for €31.7 billion," the press release details.
The European Commission said the provision of budget support will be accompanied by strict conditions regarding the rule of law, the fight against corruption, as well as economic stability and sustainable development.
Next, the European Commission's proposal for a Council implementing decision approving assistance to Ukraine for 2027 is expected to be submitted to the Council of the EU for adoption. Based on this proposal, EU member states will decide on the allocation of support within the framework of the 2027 support loan for Ukraine, specifically through Ukraine Facility, macro-financial assistance, and funding for defense and industrial capacity. As noted above, and in line with other EU financial support programs for Ukraine, this instrument includes robust safeguards and strict conditions (conditionality) regarding the rule of law, the fight against corruption, and the protection of the European Union's financial interests.
Once the Council of the EU approves the provision of this financial assistance, the European Commission will take the necessary steps to ensure that disbursements to Ukraine can begin as early as the start of 2027.

Readers gather outside Novaya Gazeta’s Moscow office after independent Russian newspaper announces closure

Lebanon court charges 13 over seized Hezbollah explosives truck
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
16:17:30 UTC
01:17:30 KST

Breadcrumb
Lebanese military court judge charges 13 over a seized Hezbollah explosives truck
A judge at a Lebanese military court charged 13 people over a truck carrying explosives belonging to the Hezbollah militant group that was seized by authorities earlier this month, state media reported Friday.
Two of the defendants were arrested when the shipment was seized and are in custody. The others remain at large and were charged in absentia. Five of the defendants were listed only by nicknames because their real names are still unknown.
The cases were referred to the military court’s investigative judge Claude Ghanem.
The charges include crimes against internal state security and possessing weapons and explosives and forming illegal associations aimed at undermining the authority of the state, the state-run National News Agency said.
There was no immediate comment from Hezbollah.
The truck, which was stopped at a checkpoint on the main highway linking Beirut with the country's east earlier in October, was carrying 780 kilograms (1,720 pounds) of explosives, including 250 kilograms (550 pounds) of TNT and 250 kilograms (550 pounds) of C-4 plastic explosives, according to judicial officials.
The news of its seizure generated heated public discussion, with many accusing Hezbollah of planning to carry out assassinations of domestic opponents at a time when the group is under increasing pressure to disarm.
Hezbollah later issued a statement acknowledging that the explosives belonged to the militant group. It said they were intended for use against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. It said it had requested Lebanese authorities return the explosives and release the two people who were detained.
Cross-border fire between Hezbollah and Israel began in October 2023, before escalating into a major war in autumn 2024.
For years, Hezbollah had been able to move weapons freely in parts of Lebanon. That changed in early March 2026, when the group fired rockets into northern Israel in support of Tehran, two days after Israel and the United States launched their war against Iran.
Hours after Hezbollah's rocket fire, the Lebanese government declared all military activities by the group "illegal". The decision came as the latest escalation developed into a war that has killed nearly 4,000 people in Lebanon and resulted in Israeli forces occupying large parts of southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah has refused to recognise the government decision outlawing its military wing.
